promotionalText: Make room for music. Slow a song down, follow its chords and lyrics, and practice one comfortable phrase at a time.
description:
Know a few guitar chords, but lose your place when the song starts? Musia connects listening, sung phrases and chord changes in a native Mac practice workspace.

HEAR ONE SMALL STEP
Play Do, Re and Mi reference tones, then try a listening quiz. Expand to a full octave when ready. The score counts your first answer, not your singing or guitar performance. These sounds work offline.

FIND A STEADY PULSE
First Pulse is a built-in synthesized 60 BPM reference with Em/Am changes. The separate metronome offers 40-160 BPM, an accented first beat and optional Em/Am changes every four beats. Start with one comfortable down-strum on beat one.

ONE PHRASE AT A TIME
Slow song playback from 0.25x to 2x while preserving pitch. Loop a lyric phrase or set A/B markers. See current/next chords, guitar finger positions, reference melody notes and the beat pulse. Keyboard playback controls keep you near your instrument.

FOLLOW WORDS AND MUSIC
Show English, Chinese and Japanese lyric tracks together, with pinyin and furigana where supplied. Translations belong to the selected vocal recording. Catalog streaming needs internet. Keep listening while the window is minimized.

KEEP PRACTICE LOCAL
Sessions and preferences stay on your Mac. Find Practice history under Settings and export or clear it when you choose. No account, microphone recording, advertising or subscription is required.

Automatically analyzed chords, beats and melody are estimates, not a verified score. Tap feedback includes device/audio latency; it does not grade instruments. Musia focuses on listening and practice, not in-app AI generation or user-upload analysis.
notes:
Native SwiftUI/AVFoundation universal Mac app, not a WebView or iOS compatibility app. Latest 0.1.2 (4) adds Do Re Mi listening practice, a 40-160 BPM metronome with Em/Am changes, EN/ZH/JA multi-select lyrics with supplied readings, and Settings > Practice history. See our App Review reply/attachment for all nine 4.3/4.2.6 answers, shared-code disclosures, founder feedback and genuine native screenshots.

No login, subscription or microphone permission.
1. Library > First Pulse: Play mode shows Em/Am fingerings. Change speed and loop a phrase. This known synthesized reference works offline.
2. Open Aya Chan / Rain of Light; play a vocal and show multiple lyric languages. Inspect readings, timed words and chords. Analyzed music data is explicitly estimated, not a verified score.
3. Lessons > Do Re Mi: play reference notes and try the first-answer listening quiz. Lessons > Metronome: choose 60 BPM, start and enable Em/Am. Leave to stop exercise clicks. No microphone or performance grade.
4. Minimize during a normal song; playback continues. Settings > Practice history contains local sessions and export/reset.

Sandbox: outgoing HTTPS and user-selected file export only, no incoming server, recording or private Studio. Creator-owned/authorized catalog, including settings of public-domain texts. Shared company infrastructure is disclosed, not another app's bundled runtime. Hosting access logs are covered by existing privacy declarations. No advertising/tracking SDK.
